comment: Committed defaults for worker assignment; settings.json in the app's userData folder overrides these workers (edit via the in-app Settings panel, or the Loop view for the two the loop uses). Providers: 'mock' (no API key needed), 'anthropic', 'openai', 'kimi' (platform or Kimi-Code key), 'openrouter' — keys saved via Settings → Providers; anthropic/openai also accept ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY from the shell. A worker may also be { provider: 'auto', model }, resolved at call time through Settings' provider priority. The executor worker is the app-wide default, used when a node template sets no worker of its own.
workersLoopComment: The loop's two workers are DECLARED here with no model, so that they are settable from the UI while their unset state stays the fail-closed one. `loop` is the model every unpinned node runs on while the loop is working a task; null means effort bands instead (DESIGN-SPEC.md §8 — a level, not a model). `reviewer` reads the diff before anything merges; null means nothing lands unattended, which is the correct default for a repo nobody has configured.
retryComment: Transient-error retry for every model call (429 / 408 / 5xx / network). A provider's own Retry-After wins when it asks for longer than the backoff; maxMs bounds any single wait so a bad hint cannot park a run.
timeoutComment: Per-attempt deadline for every model call (DESIGN-SPEC.md §8). idleMs is measured against PROGRESS, not total duration: a streaming call resets it on every emission, so a long but live stream is never cut and only silence counts. A stalled call then fails as a transient error and gets retried with a fresh deadline, instead of hanging a node forever — which attended costs a click and unattended costs the rest of the day. A non-streaming call has no progress signal, so for it this is the whole call: keep it generous. hardMs is an absolute per-attempt ceiling, null (off) by default because it would cut healthy long agent turns. The CLI-delegation providers bound their own child process and opt out of idleMs.
retrospectiveComment: The retrospective turn (DESIGN-SPEC.md §8). After an instance finishes, its completion is handed back and it is prompted ONCE more: how were the tools you had, and what was missing? A second turn rather than a tool the agent may call, because a voluntary report is a sample biased toward the models that follow instructions best, and the value here is the aggregate. It holds no tools, its output is capped, it runs after the deliverable is written, and a failure is logged and dropped — it can never fail a completed task. OFF by default: it is one extra model call per instance, and an attended user who did not ask for it should not pay for it. The loop turns it on. Point workers.retrospective at a cheap model to keep it cheap; without one it uses whichever worker did the work.
referencesComment: The reference library (DESIGN-SPEC.md §8): read-only shallow clones of repositories that already solved problems this harness keeps hitting, greppable by agents through search_references and readable through read_file with a 'reference:<repo>/<path>' prefix. Recipes, not dependencies — nothing here is vendored, and there is no write path to the library at all. App-level rather than per project, because prior art is portable in the way a backlog is not. `flyt ref update` clones or refreshes it (that reaches the network); referenceRoot overrides where it lives, always outside every repository. Each entry needs an `about` saying what the repo is good FOR: a name and a URL is a bibliography, and the point of this is not being one.

referencesExample.name: some-repo
referencesExample.about: what it is good for, concretely

benchmarkComment: The benchmark (DESIGN-SPEC.md §8): the fixed suite in <repo>/benchmark/*.bench.md, run against a THROWAWAY CLONE so that 'improve yourself' can be told apart from churn. Each case carries a probe — an independent command the harness runs after the change has landed — because the gates are part of the repo the loop is editing and therefore measure the loop's own idea of done; `landed` and `verified` end up as different numbers and the gap between them is the point. Scores land in .flyt/scores/ and are copied into .flyt/archive/<date>/ by `flyt archive write`. benchmarkRoot overrides where clones live; the default is under the user's home, outside every repository, and they are deleted afterwards unless --keep. Nothing here is configured per project: the suite IS the configuration, and it is version-controlled with the code it scores.
loopComment: The autonomous loop (DESIGN-SPEC.md §8). push: after a task's gates pass, a reviewer approves and the post-merge canary is green, push the base branch and the task branch to origin. OFF by default because pushing is outward-facing and hard to take back — a repo with no origin is still a perfectly good local loop. workers.reviewer is what reads the diff before anything merges: with none configured NOTHING lands unattended, which is the correct default for an unconfigured repo. worktreeRoot overrides where worktrees live; they are always outside the repository. minLevel is the floor under every task's effort band (DESIGN-SPEC.md §8): a repo can refuse to run its work on the cheapest tier without editing every task. allowedModels narrows what OpenRouter's Auto Router may pick, e.g. ["anthropic/*"] — empty means no restriction. caps are the three ceilings (DESIGN-SPEC.md §8), all null (off) by default: taskUsd parks a task that has spent its allowance, softUsd stops the loop ESCALATING, hardUsd finishes the in-flight node and stops the loop. They are rolling over windowMs, not calendar-daily, so a run that starts at 22:00 does not get a fresh allowance at midnight. Cost comes from what the provider reported; prices is an optional fallback table ({"provider/model": {"in": 3, "out": 15}} per million tokens) for providers that report nothing, and anything priced from it is marked estimated. autoApprove lists the gate kinds the loop may answer itself: "pre" is a node's requiresApproval ("does this plan look right?"), which the loop may answer because the landing sequence judges the actual change afterwards; "escalation" and "tool" are deliberately absent, since those are the decisions the loop exists to defer. levels: false runs on the configured workers instead of OpenRouter cost bands.
categoryWorkersComment: Optional per-category model routing: a node declaring a category resolves here before falling back to workers.executor (FLOW_NODES.md). EMPTY on purpose. This map is read from this file only and is NOT overridable from Settings, so whatever it names is pinned: it shipped mapping every category to 'mock', which silently forced each categorised work node onto the mock provider no matter what key the user saved — a real run just produced '(mock output)'. Empty means categories follow the executor worker, so one Settings change points the whole app at a real model. See categoryWorkersExample to pin one deliberately.
